x: Three new names are appearing regularly in recent results---Bob Picton (20) Mike Hamlin (20) and Chas Capener (19). Jack Goswell is enthusiastic about their potential and considers that with Gerry Cameron (still only 20) we have a quartet worth watching.
Charlie Capener was taking part in his first Open '7'. Bill Belderson was first M.P.A.A. member not gaining another award and Percy Wilson was 3rd in the Vets handicap.
New member Gerald Johnson did well to finish 81st in 65:19. Pat Duncan, Charlie Capener and Bob Picton are now beginning to move thro' the fields and faster times are in store.
At the shorter distances Charlie Capener could also make good progress in 12 months. What a pity more of our walkers can't reach a peak for the National events like Ray Middleton.
Charlie Capener holds the junior (under 21) Olympic Cup this year after clocking the good time of 35.20. It was a pity, though, that our membership does not provide him with any opposition.
Fotheringham (91:22) was 33rd, one place ahead of C. Yescombe(92:02) and four places up on C.

Another unable to get his legs going quick enough in these 'sprints' is that other well known international distance man, Don Thompson, who finished 5th on this occasion. The only other Belgrave positions to hand at time of press are 59, C.

Ray has recently been giving encouragement to Charlie Capener, who is also in the postal service, by joining him twice a week for training. Chas. has the ability to put this help to very good use and his progress will be watched with interest.
